# When the official interface and prior calls are needed for the full dJ/dq tensor of end-effector frame Jacobian in Pinocchio,

> **Current answer:** Pinocchio 4 provides getFrameKinematicHessian. First, run computeJointKinematicHessians to fill the data, then call getFrameKinematicHessian with frame_id and reference frame. The official header file returns a 6×nv×nv tensor, but no dynamic allocation requires the caller to zero out the same-sized tensor. Since no user numerical retesting has been done, the finite difference check should still be performed in the target version. The original thread does not have user numerical retesting, so the target version should still verify the available overload.

## Key terms

- Kinematic Hessian (运动学 Hessian)
- Frame Jacobian derivative (帧雅可比导数)
- Reference frame (参考坐标系)

## Problem and symptoms

- How to obtain the full dJ/dq tensor for the end-effector frame Jacobian when only the joint Hessian interface is available in Pinocchio?
- The old usage can call getJointKinematicHessian, but no equivalent getFrameKinematicHessian for frame_id is found.

## Environment

- The original post points to Pinocchio 4; the current source code verification is fixed in the devel commit 031ebb13a637babd0705ce030ce9fb2e1e9aae2c.

## Priority diagnostics

- Distinguish between needing a full 6×nv×nv dJ/dq or just Hessian-vector/wrench contraction; the most suitable algorithm differs.
- Verify the availability of getFrameKinematicHessian overload and binding in the target installation version's kinematics-derivatives.hpp.

## Possible causes

- The capability was not publicly available in early Pinocchio but was added in Pinocchio 4.

## Attempts

- The original post references an old #867 discussion where joint Hessian or repeated time-variation was used to construct the result history.

## Effective fixes

- In Pinocchio 4, first call computeJointKinematicHessians, then call getFrameKinematicHessian(model, data, frame_id, reference_frame, tensor), or use the overload that returns the tensor.
- The overload without dynamic allocation requires the caller to zero out the 6×nv×nv tensor; the return value overload creates a tensor of the same size.

## Result

- The maintainer pointed to the implemented official function on 2026-07-28, and Issue is closed as completed; the fixed commit's header file includes the frame_id overload.
